context.title: The Table of Nations
context.summary: The descendants of Noah's sons Japheth, Ham and Shem spread out and become the peoples, languages and nations of the known world.
context.background: Many names here are peoples or places Israel knew: Mizraim is Egypt, Javan the Greeks, Madai the Medes, Cush the land south of Egypt. Jewish tradition counted about seventy nations in this list. Nimrod, 'a mighty hunter before the LORD' (v. 9), is linked to Babel and Nineveh, the future great cities of Babylon and Assyria.
watchFor: Each section closes by family, language, land and nation (vv. 5, 20, 31).
Nimrod's kingdom-building (vv. 8–12) sets up the Babel story in chapter 11.
Peleg is named because 'in his days was the earth divided' (v. 25).

people.name: Noah
people.summary: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death.

people.name: Shem
people.summary: A name; renown, the first mentioned of the sons of Noah (Gen. 5:32; 6:10). He was probably the eldest of Noah’s sons. The words “brother of Japheth the elder” in Gen. 10:21 are more correctly rendered “the elder brother of Japheth,” as in the Revised Version.

people.name: Ham
people.summary: Warm, hot, and hence the south; also an Egyptian word meaning “black”, the youngest son of Noah (Gen. 5:32; comp. 9:22, 24).

people.name: Japheth
people.summary: Wide spreading: “God shall enlarge Japheth” (Heb. Yaphat Elohim le-Yephet, Gen. 9:27. Some, however, derive the name from yaphah, “to be beautiful;” hence white), one of the sons of Noah, mentioned last in order (Gen. 5:32; 6:10; 7:13), perhaps first by birth (10:21; comp. 9:24).

people.name: Tubal
people.summary: The fifth son of Japheth (Gen. 10:2).

people.name: Javan
people.summary: The fourth “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), whose descendants settled in Greece, i.e., Ionia, which bears the name of Javan in Hebrew. Alexander the Great is called the “king of Javan” (rendered “Grecia,” Dan. 8:21; 10:20; comp. 11:2; Zech. 9:13).

people.name: Meshech
people.summary: Drawing out, the sixth son of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the founder of a tribe (1 Chr. 1:5; Ezek. 27:13; 38:2, 3). They were in all probability the Moschi, a people inhabiting the Moschian Mountains, between the Black and the Caspian Seas.

people.name: Gomer
people.summary: The eldest son of Japheth, and father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah (Gen. 10:2, 3), whose descendants formed the principal branch of the population of South-eastern Europe.

people.name: Magog
people.summary: Region of Gog, the second of the “sons” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5). In Ezekiel (38:2; 39:6) it is the name of a nation, probably some Scythian or Tartar tribe descended from Japheth.

people.name: Madai
people.summary: Middle land, the third “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the name by which the Medes are known on the Assyrian monuments.

people.name: Tiras
people.summary: The youngest of the sons of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5).

people.name: Togarmah
people.summary: A son of Gomer, and grandson of Japheth (Gen. 10:3).

people.name: Ashkenaz
people.summary: One of the three sons of Gomer (Gen. 10:3), and founder of one of the tribes of the Japhetic race.

people.name: Riphath
people.summary: A crusher, Gomer’s second son (Gen. 10:3), supposed to have been the ancestor of the Paphlagonians.

people.name: Dodanim
people.summary: Leaders, a race descended from Javan (Gen. 10:4). They are known in profane history as the Dardani, originally inhabiting Illyricum. They were a semi-Pelasgic race, and in the ethnographical table (Gen. 10) they are grouped with the Chittim.

people.name: Elishah
people.summary: The oldest of the four sons of Javan (Gen. 10:4), whose descendants peopled Greece. It has been supposed that Elishah’s descendants peopled the Peloponnesus, which was known by the name of Elis.

people.name: Tarshish
people.summary: One of the “sons” of Javan (Gen. 10:4; 1 Chr. 1:7).

people.name: Canaan
people.summary: The fourth son of Ham (Gen. 10:6). His descendants were under a curse in consequence of the transgression of his father (9:22-27). His eldest son, Zidon, was the father of the Sidonians and Phoenicians.

people.name: Cush
people.summary: A son, probably the eldest, of Ham, and the father of Nimrod (Gen. 10:8; 1 Chr. 1:10). From him the land of Cush seems to have derived its name.

people.name: Mizraim
people.summary: The dual form of matzor, meaning a “mound” or “fortress,” the name of a people descended from Ham (Gen. 10:6, 13; 1 Chr. 1:8, 11). It was the name generally given by the Hebrews to the land of Egypt, and may denote the two Egypts, the Upper and the Lower.

people.name: Phut
people.summary: One of the sons of Ham (Gen. 10:6).

people.name: Dedan
people.summary: A son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7). His descendants are mentioned in Isa. 21:13, and Ezek. 27:15.

people.name: Havilah
people.summary: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

people.name: Raamah
people.summary: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

people.name: Sabtah
people.summary: Rest, the third son of Cush (Gen. 10:7; 1 Chr. 1:9).

people.name: Sabtecha
people.summary: The fifth son of Cush.

people.name: Seba
people.summary: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

people.name: Sheba
people.summary: Heb. shebha, the son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7), whose descendants settled with those of Dedan on the Persian Gulf.

people.name: Nimrod
people.summary: Firm, a descendant of Cush, the son of Ham. He was the first who claimed to be a “mighty one in the earth.” Babel was the beginning of his kingdom, which he gradually enlarged (Gen. 10:8-10).

people.name: Asshur
people.summary: Second son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17). He went from the land of Shinar and built Nineveh, etc. (Gen. 10:11, 12). He probably gave his name to Assyria, which is the usual translation of the word, although the form Asshur is sometimes retained (Num. 24:22, 24; Ezek. 27:23, etc.).

people.name: Anamim
people.summary: The name of an Egyptian tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11).

people.name: Ludim
people.summary: Probably the same as Lud (2) (comp. Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11).

people.name: Naphtuhim
people.summary: A Hamitic tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13). Others identify this word with Napata, the name of the city and territory on the southern frontier of Mizraim, the modern Meroe, at the great bend of the Nile at Soudan.

people.name: Casluhim
people.summary: Fortified, a people descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:14; 1 Chr. 1:12).

people.name: Heth
people.summary: Dread, a descendant of Canaan, and the ancestor of the Hittites (Gen. 10:18; Deut. 7:1), who dwelt in the vicinity of Hebron (Gen. 23:3, 7).

people.name: Zidon
people.summary: A fishery, a town on the Mediterranean coast, about 25 miles north of Tyre. It received its name from the “first-born” of Canaan, the grandson of Noah (Gen. 10:15, 19).

people.name: Amorite
people.summary: Highlanders, or hillmen, the name given to the descendants of one of the sons of Canaan (Gen. 14:7), called Amurra or Amurri in the Assyrian and Egyptian inscriptions.

people.name: Girgasite
people.summary: Dwelling in clayey soil, the descendants of the fifth son of Canaan (Gen. 10:16), one of the original tribes inhabiting the land of Canaan before the time of the Israelites (Gen. 15:21; Deut. 7:1).

people.name: Jebusite
people.summary: The name of the original inhabitants of Jebus, mentioned frequently among the seven nations doomed to destruction (Gen. 10:16; 15:21; Ex. 3:8, 17; 13:5, etc.).

people.name: Hivite
people.summary: One of the original tribes scattered over Palestine, from Hermon to Gibeon in the south. The name is interpreted as “midlanders” or “villagers” (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15).

people.name: Arkite
people.summary: (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15), a designation of certain descendants from the Phoenicians or Sidonians, the inhabitants of Arka, 12 miles north of Tripoli, opposite the northern extremity of Lebanon.

people.name: Sinite
people.summary: An inhabitant of Sin, near Arka (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15).

people.name: Zemarite
people.summary: The designation of one of the Phoenician tribes (Gen. 10:18) who inhabited the town of Sumra, at the western base of the Lebanon range.

people.name: Eber
people.summary: The third post-duluvian patriach after Shem (Gen. 10:24; 11:14). He is regarded as the founder of the Hebrew race (10:21; Num. 24:24).

people.name: Arphaxad
people.summary: Son of Shem, born the year after the Deluge. He died at the age of 438 years (Gen. 11:10-13; 1 Chr. 1:17, 18; Luke 3:36). He dwelt in Mesopotamia, and became, according to the Jewish historian Josephus, the progenitor of the Chaldeans.

people.name: Aram
people.summary: The son of Shem (Gen. 10:22); according to Gen. 22:21, a grandson of Nahor.

people.name: Elam
people.summary: Highland, the son of Shem (Gen. 10:22), and the name of the country inhabited by his descendants (14:1, 9; Isa. 11:11; 21:2, etc.) lying to the east of Babylonia, and extending to the shore of the Mediterranean, a distance in a direct line of about 1,000 miles.

people.name: Lud
people.summary: The fourth son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17), ancestor of the Lydians probably.

people.name: Hul
people.summary: Circle, the second son of Aram (Gen. 10:23), and grandson of Shem.

people.name: Mash
people.summary: (= Meshech 1 Chr. 1:17), one of the four sons of Aram, and the name of a tribe descended from him (Gen. 10:23) inhabiting some part probably of Mesopotamia.

people.name: Uz
people.summary: The son of Aram, and grandson of Shem (Gen. 10:23; 1 Chr. 1:17).

people.name: Salah
people.summary: A shoot, a descendant of Arphaxed (Luke 3:35, 36); called also Shelah (1 Chr. 1:18, 24).

people.name: Peleg
people.summary: Division, one of the sons of Eber; so called because “in his days was the earth divided” (Gen. 10:25). Possibly he may have lived at the time of the dispersion from Babel.

people.name: Joktan
people.summary: Little, the second of the two sons of Eber (Gen. 10:25; 1 Chr. 1:19). There is an Arab tradition that Joktan (Arab.

people.name: Almodad
people.summary: Immeasurable, the first named of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:26), the founder of an Arabian tribe.

people.name: Hazarmaveth
people.summary: Court of death, the third son of Joktan, and a region in Arabia-Felix settled by him (Gen. 10:26; 1 Chr. 1:20).

people.name: Hadoram
people.summary: The fifth son of Joktan, the founder of an Arab tribe (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21).

people.name: Uzal
people.summary: A wanderer, a descendant of Joktan (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21), the founder apparently of one of the Arab tribes; the name also probably of the province they occupied and of their chief city.

people.name: Abimael
people.summary: Father of Mael, one of the sons or descendants of Joktan, in Northern Arabia (Gen. 10:28; 1 Chr. 1:22).

people.name: Ebal
people.summary: A descendant of Eber (1 Chr. 1:22), called also Obal (Gen. 10:28).

people.name: Sheba
people.summary: Heb. id.

people.name: Havilah
people.summary: A son of Joktan (Gen. 10:29; 1 Chr. 1:23).

people.name: Jobab
people.summary: One of the sons of Joktan, and founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 10:29).

people.name: Ophir
people.summary: One of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:29).

places.name: Accad
places.summary: The high land or mountains, a city in the land of Shinar. It has been identified with the mounds of Akker Kuf, some 50 miles to the north of Babylon; but this is doubtful.

places.name: Babel
places.summary: The name given to the tower which the primitive fathers of our race built in the land of Shinar after the Deluge (Gen. 11:1-9). Their object in building this tower was probably that it might be seen as a rallying-point in the extensive plain of Shinar, to which they had emigrated from the uplands of Armenia, and so prevent their being scattered abroad.

places.name: Calneh
places.summary: Fort, one of the four cities founded by Nimrod (Gen. 10:10). It is the modern Niffer, a lofty mound of earth and rubbish situated in the marshes on the left, i.e., the east, bank of the Euphrates, but 30 miles distant from its present course, and about 60 miles south-south-east from Babylon.

places.name: Erech
places.summary: (LXX., “Orech”), length, or Moon-town, one of the cities of Nimrod’s kingdom in the plain of Shinar (Gen. 10:10); the Orchoe of the Greeks and Romans.

places.name: Shinar
places.summary: LXX. and Vulgate “Senaar;” in the inscriptions, “Shumir;” probably identical with Babylonia or Southern Mesopotamia, extending almost to the Persian Gulf.

places.name: Assyria
places.summary: The name derived from the city Asshur on the Tigris, the original capital of the country, was originally a colony from Babylonia, and was ruled by viceroys from that kingdom.

places.name: Calah
places.summary: One of the most ancient cities of Assyria. “Out of that land he [i.e., Nimrod] went forth into Assyria, and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah, and Resen” (Gen. 10:11, R.V.).

places.name: Nineveh
places.summary: First mentioned in Gen. 10:11, which is rendered in the Revised Version, “He [i.e., Nimrod] went forth into Assyria and builded Nineveh.” It is not again noticed till the days of Jonah, when it is described (Jonah 3:3; 4:11) as a great and populous city, the flourishing capital of the Assyrian empire (2 Kings 19:36; Isa. 37:37).

places.name: Rehoboth
places.summary: Named among the cities of Asshur (Gen. 10:11).

places.name: Resen
places.summary: Head of the stream; bridle, one of Nimrod’s cities (Gen. 10:12), “between Nineveh and Calah.” It has been supposed that the four cities named in this verse were afterwards combined into one under the name of Nineveh.

places.name: Admah
places.summary: Earth, one of the five cities of the vale of Siddim (Gen. 10:19). It was destroyed along with Sodom and Gomorrah (19:24; Deut. 29:23).

places.name: Gaza
places.summary: Called also Azzah, which is its Hebrew name (Deut. 2:23; 1 Kings 4:24; Jer. 25:20), strong, a city on the Mediterranean shore, remarkable for its early importance as the chief centre of a great commercial traffic with Egypt.

places.name: Gerar
places.summary: A region; lodging-place, a very ancient town and district in the south border of Palestine, which was ruled over by a king named Abimelech (Gen. 10:19; 20:1, 2).

places.name: Gomorrah
places.summary: Submersion, one of the five cities of the plain of Siddim which were destroyed by fire (Gen. 10:19; 13:10; 19:24, 28). These cities probably stood close together, and were near the northern extremity of what is now the Dead Sea.

places.name: Lasha
places.summary: Fissure, a place apparently east of the Dead Sea (Gen. 10:19).

places.name: Sidon
places.summary: A fishery, a town on the Mediterranean coast, about 25 miles north of Tyre. It received its name from the “first-born” of Canaan, the grandson of Noah (Gen. 10:15, 19).

places.name: Sodom
places.summary: Burning; the walled, a city in the vale of Siddim (Gen. 13:10; 14:1-16). The wickedness of its inhabitants brought down upon it fire from heaven, by which it was destroyed (18:16-33; 19:1-29; Deut. 23:17).

places.name: Zeboiim
places.summary: One of the “five cities of the plain” of Sodom, generally coupled with Admah (Gen. 10:19; 14:2; Deut. 29:23; Hos. 11:8). It had a king of its own (Shemeber), and was therefore a place of some importance.

places.name: Mesha
places.summary: A plain in that part of the boundaries of Arabia inhabited by the descendants of Joktan (Gen. 10:30).

places.name: Sephar
places.summary: Numbering, (Gen. 10:30), supposed by some to be the ancient Himyaritic capital, “Shaphar,” Zaphar, on the Indian Ocean, between the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea.

events.title: Nimrod's kingdom begins
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 10:8–12. People: Nimrod. Place: Shinar, Assyria, Accad, Babel.
